name: Circuit of the Americas

sources.geometry: OpenStreetMap highway=raceway ways (ODbL, Overpass API), Taubin-smoothed; start line located on USGS NAIP orthophoto (imagery.nationalmap.gov USGSNAIPPlus)
sources.width: Published/approximate: ~15 m standard (COTA/FIA circuit facts), widening sharply into Turn 1 (fan-shaped, capped at 24 m centreline width) and at the Turn 12 braking zone; ~13-14 m through esses and stadium section
sources.elevation: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM via EPQS (https://epqs.nationalmap.gov/v1/json), centreline + edge samples
sources.camber: USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar DEM edge-vs-centre samples (trackkit.profile_from_samples)
sources.corners: Official F1 turn numbering: corner positions from F1 live-timing circuit data (MultiViewer API) fitted onto the centreline, apex = curvature peak within 25 m
sources.pit: OpenStreetMap way "Pit Lane" (514836373): entry after Turn 19, exit on the run from Turn 1 to Turn 2
sources.trim: Medium-high downforce: long back straight but the Turn 3-9 esses and stadium section reward downforce; teams run near Spa-level wings or slightly more
sources.pitLimit: F1 Sporting Regulations default 80 km/h (US GP event notes); WEC Lone Star Le Mans 60 km/h pit-lane limit (WEC sporting regs)
sources.pitLoss: F1 green-flag pit loss from F1 live-timing derived circuit data (MultiViewer API api.multiviewer.app/api/v1/circuits/9/2026: normal 20.81 s, SC 13.50 s); WEC unknown, omitted
sources.raceLaps: F1 2026 United States GP: 56 laps (not a sprint weekend in 2026; 2026 sprints: China, Miami, Canada, Britain, Netherlands, Singapore)

notes: Anticlockwise. Start/finish timing line measured on NAIP imagery opposite the pit building. Turn 1 is the steep uphill left-hander at the top of the hill. 3DEP lidar gives Turn 1 ~27 m above the start line and a 31 m lap range (the often-quoted 41 m/133 ft is not reproduced by lidar or Copernicus on the racing surface). Widths are approximate published values, not measured.
